record.original_question: (M. Bridson). Let Fm be a free group of rank m and let ϕ ∈ Aut(Fm) be a polynomially growing automorphism of maximal degree m − 1, which means that for some(equivalently, any) free basis {x1,..., xm } of Fm, the sequence maxi |ϕn(xi)| grows at the rate of nm−1, where |g| denotes the minimal length of g in the xi and their inverses. a) Is the free-by-cyclic group Fm ⋊ϕ Z virtually special? b) In particular, are the Hydra groups Gm = Fm ⋊ Z = ⟨a1,..., am, t | t−1 a1 t = a1, t−1 ai t = ai ai−1 for all i > 1⟩ virtually special?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m \geq 2$ be an integer and let $F_m$ denote the free group of rank $m$ with free basis $\{x_1,\dots,x_m\}$. For $g \in F_m$, let $|g|$ denote the minimal length of a word representing $g$ in the letters $x_1^{\pm 1},\dots,x_m^{\pm 1}$.

An automorphism $\varphi \in \mathrm{Aut}(F_m)$ is said to be polynomially growing of maximal degree $m-1$ if, for some (equivalently, every) free basis $\{x_1,\dots,x_m\}$ of $F_m$, one has
$$\max_{1 \leq i \leq m} |\varphi^n(x_i)| \asymp n^{m-1} \quad \text{as } n \to \infty.$$

A group $G$ is called virtually special if it has a finite-index subgroup that embeds as a subgroup of a right-angled Artin group (equivalently, the fundamental group of a special cube complex in the sense of Haglund–Wise).

(a) For every such polynomially growing automorphism $\varphi$ of maximal degree $m-1$, is the free-by-cyclic group $F_m \rtimes_\varphi \mathbb{Z}$ virtually special?

(b) In particular, consider the Hydra groups
$$G_m = \langle a_1,\dots,a_m,\, t \mid t^{-1} a_1 t = a_1,\ t^{-1} a_i t = a_i a_{i-1}\ \text{for all } i>1 \rangle,$$
each of which is a free-by-cyclic group of the form $F_m \rtimes \mathbb{Z}$ with monodromy a polynomially growing automorphism of maximal degree $m-1$. Are the Hydra groups $G_m$ virtually special?
artifact.category_tag: Geometric group theory: virtually special groups
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed by M. Bridson, appears in the 2026 Kourovka Notebook as a new problem and seems to remain open. Recent work (e.g., torsion homology growth of polynomially growing free-by-cyclic groups, and constructions by Kudlinska and others) has produced virtually special analogues of Hydra-like groups where the rank-2 abelian piece is replaced by a more complicated RAAG, and progress has been made on subgroup separability of free-by-cyclic groups, but the Hydra groups $G_m$ themselves and the general polynomially-growing maximal-degree case have not been confirmed virtually special in the sources found.

status_evidence.title: Torsion homology growth of polynomially growing free-by-cyclic groups
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs virtually special free-by-cyclic groups F_{2m} ⋊ Z with polynomially growing monodromy of degree m, as analogues of Hydra groups, leaving the original Hydra groups case open.
status_evidence.claim: Analogues of Hydra groups are virtually special, but the question for the actual Hydra groups remains open.

status_evidence.title: On subgroup separability of free-by-cyclic and deficiency 1 groups (Kudlinska)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies subgroup separability for free-by-cyclic groups, related to virtual specialness; does not settle Bridson's question for Hydra groups.
status_evidence.claim: The virtual specialness of Hydra groups and of polynomially growing free-by-cyclic groups of maximal degree is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Hydra Groups (Dison–Riley)
status_evidence.snippet: Defines the Hydra groups G_m = ⟨a_1,...,a_m,t | t^{-1}a_1 t = a_1, t^{-1}a_i t = a_i a_{i-1}⟩ and studies their distorted subgroups.
status_evidence.claim: Source for the definition of the Hydra groups featured in Bridson's question.
